text:
ryan: Quick one — customer trying to run our JS SDK in Cloudflare Workers. esbuild errors: "could not resolve 'fs'". Any minimal pattern besides telling them to add --external flags?

maya: We hit this a lot. Best UX is an explicit edge export (e.g. `redwood-inference/edge`) that is ESM-only and has zero node deps. Then bundlers pick it up without hacks.

tri: Agreed. Short checklist:
- add `./edge` in `exports` -> dist/edge.mjs + dist/edge.d.ts (DOM types)
- ensure retry code uses `globalThis.setTimeout` (no process.nextTick)
- avoid referencing `process.env` at runtime (use config object)

ryan: For TS, how do we avoid consumers accidentally pulling main index.d.ts which references Node types?

maya: Use explicit subpath import in docs: `import { createEdgeClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'`. Also map types in exports so `./edge` points to edge.d.ts. Some bundlers still pick main types but this reduces breakage.

tri: For crypto: Workers have `crypto.getRandomValues`. Provide a tiny helper `randomBytes(n): Uint8Array` in edge entry. Document it.

ryan: Wranger/wrangler v3: quick build snippet we give customers:
```
esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --outfile=dist/worker.js --platform=browser --format=esm
```
That avoids externals if they import `/edge`.

maya: Docs TODOs: add `workers-starter` example, small troubleshooting section (esbuild flags, tsconfig lib: ["dom"]) and note about large dev headers — gate them behind NODE_ENV.

build-bot: CI: branch `edge-entry` created. esbuild edge bundle ✅. Integration tests: 10/12 (two node-only tests skipped).

tri: Also consider telemetry (opt-in) when `createEdgeClient` used so we can see adoption before removing heavy deps from main entry.

ryan: Perfect. I'll draft the README snippet and a tiny starter repo. Thanks! :pray:
